flags.where: Sample response (A): 'the Royal Society when it was organized in 1662'
flags.detail: The Royal Society was organized/founded in 1660 (first formal meeting at Gresham College, 28 Nov 1660); 1662 is the date of its royal charter of incorporation. Libby's account refers to incorporation in 1662, so the sample both misstates the founding date and slightly misdescribes the source.

flags.where: Sample response (C): 'they did not have the same kind of science as Europe and were not as advanced. Science in Europe was more organized than in other regions.'
flags.detail: This is a Eurocentric and historically unsupported generalization. In 1450–1750 Asian regions had highly organized astronomical inquiry: Ulugh Beg's Samarkand observatory and madrasa (1420s–1440s), Taqi al-Din's Istanbul observatory (1577), China's state Astronomical Bureau (which also employed Jesuits), and Jai Singh II's Jantar Mantar observatories (1720s–1730s). Presenting non-European science as less 'advanced' and less organized is both inaccurate and non-neutral; even a low-tier sample should not contain false historical claims.
